## Local Considerations for Chicago Suburb Homeowners

Painting in the western Chicago suburbs carries specific considerations that generic online advice often misses.

**Illinois climate impact.** Temperature extremes from -15 to 100+ degrees Fahrenheit mean paint must flex without cracking through the full annual range. Products formulated for milder climates underperform here.

**HOA requirements.** Many Hinsdale and Lockport subdivisions require color approval before painting begins. Painting without approval can trigger fines and forced repainting - an expensive mistake. Our team navigates HOA submissions routinely and maintains current palette documentation for active subdivisions.

**Seasonal timing.** Exterior painting season runs April through October in most years. Interior painting works year-round, with winter offering lower humidity and faster dry times. Spring and fall are peak demand seasons - book 4-6 weeks ahead for these windows.

**Local building codes.** Homes built before 1978 may contain lead paint that requires EPA RRP-certified contractors for any disturbance. D&D Pro Painting maintains current RRP certification and follows all required containment and documentation protocols.

faqs.question: What is the best time of year for exterior painting in Illinois?
faqs.answer: Late April through mid-October, when overnight temperatures consistently stay above 50 degrees Fahrenheit. May through September provides the most reliable conditions. Avoid painting in direct midday sun above 90 degrees - professional crews work early mornings and shaded elevations during peak summer heat.

faqs.question: How much does exterior painting cost in the Chicago suburbs?
faqs.answer: Typical two-story homes run $6,000-$10,000 for professional work with premium paint and thorough preparation. Smaller homes start around $3,500. Estate homes in Hinsdale and Oak Brook can run $15,000-$35,000+. The biggest cost driver is preparation intensity, which directly determines how long the paint job lasts.

faqs.question: How long does professional exterior painting take?
faqs.answer: Most single-family homes take 5-10 working days including preparation, priming, and two finish coats. Larger homes and estate properties may take 2-3 weeks. Weather delays are common during Illinois spring and fall - professional contractors build buffer days into the schedule.
